name: devpty
description: A PTY SLAVE READS AND WRITES THE SAME THROUGH TWO NAMES FOR IT -- apple/fgx#198's THIRD defect, and the stateful-device case UFS 1.7d I3 step 4 records as OWED rather than skipped.  spec_chread asks a device for a BULK d_read and falls to a per-byte loop when it has none; every tty line's slot was empty, so a slave read through a device node never met the line discipline at all -- it reached _PtyS_Read, whose whole body was `LDA #EIO'.  The slots are ptsread and ptswrite now: `if (tp->t_oproc) error = (*linesw[tp->t_line].l_read)(tp, uio, flag); ptcwakeup(tp, FWRITE);' (vendor/2.11BSD/usr/sys/sys/tty_pty.c:134-137).  WHAT THE PAIR MEASURES IS AN ALIAS: /dev/ttyp0 and /dev/./ttyp0 are two DIFFERENT VNODES naming ONE device, linked on the rdev hash by checkalias and both flagged VALIASED, and spec_close turns on the difference between them -- 'vcount asks how many VNODES name this device ... returning early here is what stops one path's close tearing the driver down under another' (apple/fgx#76).  So the claim is that both names reach the same line in both directions and that holding one open does not change what the other does.  The '.' is how the second name is got: it is the cheapest way to make the resolver produce a second vnode for one device.  EVERY MEASUREMENT HAS ITS CONTROL ON THE SAME PAIR, THE SAME LINE AND THE SAME MODE, so the only difference between them is the NAME: R1/R2 the plain one, R4/R5 the alias.  Without the controls a failure could equally be the pty, the raw mode or the master.  R5 COST A STACK MOVE (apple/fgx#246): written first, it RESET THE MACHINE, because ttwrite kept upstream's char obuf[OBUFSIZ] on the kernel stack and the vnode road is deep -- this same probe reached 516 of the 512-byte per-task stack, with no guard on FGX_DP_KERNELC to catch it.  The buffer is per-task in the u-area now, which gives all 100 bytes back on EVERY tty write rather than buying one road its margin by shrinking a chunk size.  THE MODE-SETTING ioctl IS ON THE FIRST FD AND NO LONGER HAS TO BE: this said spec_ioctl PANICS on a character device, so asking through a device node would take the kernel down rather than answer.  UFS 1.7d I4 built the door (KSVC_CDIOCTL/KSVC_CDPOLL onto the chardev registry, which had been dispatching COPS_Ioctl and COPS_Poll for the registry road since T2) and routed ioctl(2) and select(2) on a far-ops descriptor over the seam.  R6 ROUND-TRIPS THROUGH ONE FD ALONE, which is NOT this probe's usual shape, and two earlier attempts are why: TIOCGETP through a device node was answered ENOTTY (measured e=25), because FGX routes the sgtty and pgrp family in the SYSCALL layer at @si_ttyX before the chardev dispatch and it never reaches a d_ioctl at all; and TIOCSLTC set on one fd followed by TIOCGLTC read on the other returned ZEROS, because both were in the syscall layer's tty list, so the set went to ttioctl's ltchars and the get came back from _PtyS_Ioctl's per-pair store -- two stores, one command name.  Upstream has no such split: ptyioctl answers its own commands and then falls through to ttioctl unconditionally (vendor/2.11BSD/usr/sys/sys/tty_pty.c), so the discipline is reached THROUGH the switch; FGX had that fall-through in the syscall layer, ABOVE where a device node enters.  That was apple/fgx#267 and it is FIXED -- the sequence is _Io_CdThenTty now, called by @kc_cdioctl.  R9 IS THE COMPARISON THAT WAS IMPOSSIBLE WHILE IT STOOD: the mode is set on the first fd at the top of main and TIOCGETP read back through the alias must return the SAME SIX BYTES, which is this probe's usual shape restored to the ioctl arm.  R6 is kept unchanged rather than rewritten to use sgtty, because TIOCGLTC/TIOCSLTC are answered by _PtyS_Ioctl's per-pair store and not by the discipline -- R6 exercises the DRIVER end of the road and R9 the DISCIPLINE end, and collapsing them would lose the driver half.  MEASURED DISCRIMINATING: point @kc_cdioctl back at _Chardev_Ioctl alone and R9 reports FAIL dev-getp e=25, which is the defect's original symptom exactly.  So R6 asks only what this increment built and asks it whole: six bytes IN through TIOCSLTC and the same six OUT through TIOCGLTC, both on the device node, exercising syscall, seam, vnode, spec arm, registry and driver in both directions.  It is still the only place on target where the ioctl arm discriminates -- ufs_devprobe says against itself that every chardev it can reach answers ENOTTY to every command, exactly what a stubbed spec_ioctl returns.  R7/R8 ARE THE SELECT PAIR AND THEY MOVE: the block they replace answered far-ops descriptors locally with 'ready for everything', right for a regular file and WRONG for a line that can block -- the same tty reached through a device node was reported readable with no key waiting.  So the assertion is a CHANGE and not a value: not readable with the queue drained, readable after the master writes one byte.  MEASURED DISCRIMINATING, both arms: restore @cl_notArm's local answer and R7 reports FAIL dev-sel-empty n=1 rf=32 -- the drained line called readable, the divergence itself; restore @si_notArm's ENOTTY and R6 reports FAIL dev-sltc e=25.  The mode belongs to the LINE, not to a descriptor, so setting it through either fd sets it for both.  RAW WITH NO ECHO because the measurement is one byte at a time: a cooked read would not return until a newline, and an echo would leave bytes in t_outq for the master reads to trip over.  MEASURED DISCRIMINATING, both slots, and the two failure modes DIFFER: restore the slave's d_read slot to 0,0,0 and R4 reports FAIL alias-in e=5 -- EIO, _PtyS_Read's stub -- with the plain-name controls still green; restore the d_write slot and R5 HANGS rather than reporting, the last line on screen being R4 with the shell prompt never returning.  Said here rather than left to be rediscovered, the way ptyrec's description says the same about its own mutation: the arithmetic predicts an EIO bubbling out of spec_chwrite's per-byte loop and the machine does something else.
